data.name: Ellipsis
data.detailed_description:
Check out our upcoming game, Sweet Surrender!

Add it to your wishlist!


Acerca do jogo


Nós criamos um lindo universo para você descobrir e explorar no seu próprio ritmo. Voe pelas fases, desviando e fugindo dos inimigos antes que eles consigam reagir. Ou então explore calmamente, dominando cada mundo e descobrindo todos os seus segredos. De um modo ou de outro, Ellipsis vai manter você ligado com surpresas do início ao fim.

“É como a melhor parte de Geometry Wars” - Tycho Brahe (Fundador do PAX, Penny Arcade)

Ellipsis foi desenvolvido com uma interface clean e minimalista e totalmente SEM texto. Ele permite que o jogador explore em seu próprio ritmo, orientando-o sutilmente, produzindo assim uma experiência pick-up-and-play incrível.

PRINCIPAIS CARACTERÍSTICAS

• Mais 150 níveis criados à mão com dificuldade crescente, dispostos em 8 mundos distintos
• Editor de níveis com suporte a Steam Workshop
• Pick-up-and-play para todas as idades
• Gráficos minimalistas exuberantes
• Sem texto - acessível a uma audiência global
• Suporte para Mouse e Touchscreen, compatível com PCs Touch 2 em 1
• Suporte para Windows, Mac e Linux

CRÉDITOS

• Desenvolvido por Yacine Salmi e Stefan Hell
• Trilha sonora por Filippo Beck Peccoz
• Comunidade e PR: Christopher Wulf and Felix Kramer
• Agradecimentos especiais a Alex Zacherl, Johannes Roth e Max Wandinger

Um grande OBRIGADO a você, jogador.

data.short_description: Ellipsis é um jogo de ação Avoid ’Em Up com um visual neon minimalista mas poderoso. Controle a sua espaçonave através de um universo misterioso desviando habilmente de hordas de inimigos errantes, lanças, raios laser entre outros.

reviews.review:
Ellipsis is one of those indie games that demonstrates how much can be accomplished with a focused idea and a strong sense of style. Developed and published by Salmi Games, the title takes an unconventional approach to arcade design by stripping away combat almost entirely and replacing it with a constant emphasis on movement, timing, and survival. At first glance, its minimalist visuals and simple controls may suggest a casual experience, but beneath that clean exterior lies a surprisingly demanding and rewarding game that steadily challenges players to think differently about the genre.

The game's central premise revolves around guiding a small entity through dangerous environments filled with hostile obstacles and unpredictable hazards. Instead of eliminating enemies, players are tasked with avoiding them while navigating increasingly intricate levels. This "avoid 'em up" concept gives Ellipsis a unique identity, transforming every stage into a puzzle of positioning and reflexes. The absence of text throughout the experience is another notable design decision. Everything is communicated visually, from mechanics to progression, allowing players to immerse themselves without interruption while making the game universally accessible regardless of language.

Salmi Games has packed the adventure with more than 150 handcrafted levels spread across eight distinct regions, and the variety between them helps maintain momentum from beginning to end. New enemy behaviors, environmental mechanics, and hazards are introduced at a measured pace, ensuring that players are consistently learning. What begins as a relaxing journey soon becomes an intense test of precision, requiring split-second decisions and a keen awareness of surroundings. The gradual escalation of difficulty is handled effectively, though some later stages may prove frustrating for players who prefer a more forgiving experience.

One of Ellipsis' greatest strengths is its presentation. The game embraces a minimalist art style built around vibrant colors and geometric shapes, creating environments that feel abstract yet memorable. Each world carries its own visual personality, preventing the experience from becoming repetitive despite its relatively simple assets. Complementing the visuals is an atmospheric soundtrack that reinforces the game's mysterious tone. Together, the art and audio create an experience that feels almost hypnotic, drawing players into its world while maintaining a sense of tension during more demanding encounters.

Beyond the main campaign, Ellipsis offers additional value through its level editor and Steam Workshop integration. Players can design and share their own stages, significantly expanding the amount of available content and encouraging community creativity. Support for multiple control methods, including controllers, mouse input, and touchscreens, also reflects the developer's commitment to accessibility. These features help the game remain relevant long after the final official level has been completed.

While Ellipsis succeeds in many areas, it may not appeal to everyone. Its minimalist philosophy extends beyond its visuals and affects the overall experience, meaning players looking for a rich narrative, character development, or elaborate progression systems may come away wanting more. Likewise, the game's singular focus on avoidance can occasionally feel repetitive during extended sessions. However, these limitations are largely a matter of personal preference rather than flaws in execution.

In the end, Ellipsis stands as a thoughtful and polished indie title that confidently embraces its own identity. It proves that compelling gameplay does not always require complexity, and that a simple concept executed with care can leave a lasting impression. With its elegant design, satisfying challenge, and wealth of handcrafted content, it remains a standout example of minimalist game development done right.

Rating: 8/10
